question: Can diffusion sampling time be reparameterized by conditional information loss so that uniform solver steps spend equal resolution on data-relevant denoising stages?

key_findings.claim: Conditional entropy defines a data-dependent time coordinate invariant to the original parameterization of an equivalent diffusion SDE.
key_findings.evidence: The paper uses H[x0|xt], whose derivative is determined by score norms, and proves it is a proper monotone time change. Equivalent SDEs mapped into entropic time have the identity as their remaining time transformation.

key_findings.claim: The entropy-rate curve can be estimated with a pretrained denoiser's standard squared error, but that estimate is an upper bound on the true rate.
key_findings.evidence: I-MMSE connects conditional-entropy production to denoising MMSE. Replacing the optimal score with the learned network introduces a nonnegative score-error gap, so model error mixes irreducible data uncertainty with denoiser imperfection.

key_findings.claim: Rescaling the entropy rate is essential for continuous image data; raw entropic time often fails visually.
key_findings.evidence: Differential conditional entropy diverges toward negative infinity as t approaches zero. The proposed integral of sigma times the entropy rate matches the analytic isotropic-Gaussian optimum and produces usable schedules, whereas raw entropic schedules yield unrecognizable image samples and are omitted from the main image tables.

key_findings.claim: On first-order DDIM sampling, rescaled-entropy grids substantially improve low-step image metrics over the pretrained models' EDM grids.
key_findings.evidence: For FFHQ stochastic DDIM at 16/32/64 evaluations, FID changes from 40.48/21.63/10.62 to 30.81/14.89/7.60; the spectral variant reaches 30.61/14.60/7.33. ImageNet-512 EDM2-XXL stochastic FID changes from 30.39/8.80/3.81 to 13.38/3.83/2.60.

key_findings.claim: The schedule is solver-dependent despite being presented as a canonical information time.
key_findings.evidence: Second-order EDM and DPM-style solvers perform worse with the proposed grid. The authors attribute this to lookahead altering the relevant information-transfer definition, leaving the method validated only for first-order deterministic and stochastic DDIM in the tested regime.

method.core_idea: Estimate how quickly a noisy state loses information about its clean source and place uniform numerical-solver steps in that information coordinate rather than in hand-designed noise time.
method.mechanism: The conditional-entropy derivative is derived from the SDE score and converted to denoising squared error via I-MMSE. A pretrained denoiser estimates error on clean/noised samples over 128 time points; numerical integration produces entropy, sigma-rescaled entropy, or a Fourier-frequency-balanced spectral curve. Uniform points on the normalized curve are interpolated back to the original noise schedule and supplied to DDIM without retraining.
assumptions: Equal increments of conditional entropy allocate first-order discretization error efficiently.
The pretrained denoiser's squared error is close enough to optimal MMSE to recover a useful data-information curve.
The isotropic-Gaussian-derived sigma rescaling transfers to multimodal natural images.
FID/FD-DINO changes reflect schedule quality rather than metric-specific or brightness artifacts.

techniques.role: Defines a canonical data-dependent diffusion clock.
Estimates information loss from denoising squared error.
Regularizes continuous-data behavior and recovers the Gaussian-optimal coordinate.
Reweights Fourier directions so different image frequencies influence the grid.
Uses the estimated curve with existing pretrained models and solvers.

evaluations.setting: Analytic discrete points and Gaussian mixtures sampled with stochastic DDIM.
evaluations.metric: KL divergence versus number of generation steps.
evaluations.result: Raw entropic time is strongest for discrete/well-separated modes, while rescaled entropy is strongest once Gaussian components overlap.
evaluations.baseline: Uniform original time and the alternate entropy parameterizations.

evaluations.setting: Pretrained EDM on CIFAR-10/FFHQ and EDM2 on ImageNet-64/512 with deterministic and stochastic first-order DDIM, 16-64 evaluations.
evaluations.metric: FID and FD-DINOv2 over 50,000 generated images.
evaluations.result: Rescaled schedules usually improve low-NFE quality; FFHQ stochastic FID at 32 steps improves 21.63 to 14.89 and ImageNet-512 XXL stochastic FID 8.80 to 3.83.
evaluations.baseline: The pretrained EDM/EDM2 sampling schedule at the same model, solver, and NFE.

evaluations.setting: Second-order diffusion solvers using the same entropic grids.
evaluations.metric: Generation quality relative to the standard EDM grid.
evaluations.result: The entropic schedules are worse, motivating a solver-aware information coordinate.
evaluations.baseline: Standard schedule with the same second-order solver.

limitations: The optimality theorem covers Gaussian data and deterministic DDIM, not natural images or the proposed rescaled heuristic generally.
Learned denoiser error biases the entropy-rate estimate upward in a time-dependent way.
Raw entropic time fails on continuous images and main tables retain only the successful rescaled variant.
Second-order solvers degrade, so the coordinate is not universal across numerical integration methods.
Schedule estimation requires dataset samples and extra denoiser evaluations, though it is amortized and training-free.
No matched comparison against learned timestep optimizers or modern solver-specific schedule tuning is reported across all datasets.
failure_modes: A weak denoiser can concentrate steps where its own error is large rather than where the true reverse process is difficult.
Differential-entropy divergence near clean data destabilizes raw entropic grids.
Frequency balancing can overweight low-amplitude or metric-irrelevant image modes.
A schedule optimized for one checkpoint, guidance strength, or solver may not transfer to another.
Brightness shifts can improve or worsen FID independently of semantic fidelity.
reusable_insights: Treat a timestep grid as a coordinate choice before optimizing individual points separately for every step count.
Use analytic Gaussian cases to identify candidate invariant coordinates and sanity-check samplers.
Decompose estimated information rate into irreducible uncertainty and model approximation error.
Report raw and regularized versions when differential-information quantities diverge at endpoints.
Design schedules jointly with solver order because lookahead changes which local error matters.
open_questions: Is there an entropy-like coordinate with a provable global error bound for nonlinear data distributions?
How should conditional information be defined for multistep and higher-order solvers?
Can the rate be estimated independently of model error using multiple denoisers or held-out score diagnostics?
Does entropic training-time sampling improve training efficiency as well as inference grids?
How does classifier-free guidance change the relevant conditional-entropy curve?

competitive_landscape.title: Align Your Steps: Optimizing Sampling Schedules in Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Align Your Steps directly optimizes discrete sampling times and supplies the Gaussian schedule that motivates this work. Entropic time replaces per-NFE optimization with one data-dependent coordinate estimated from denoising error, but loses direct objective optimality on real data.

competitive_landscape.title: Beta Sampling Is All You Need: Efficient Image Generation Strategy for Diffusion Models Using Stepwise Spectral Analysis
competitive_landscape.difference: Beta Sampling uses stepwise spectral behavior to prioritize image-generation times. The target derives a global information coordinate and adds a spectral entropy variant, offering stronger information-theoretic motivation but not a comprehensive head-to-head comparison.

competitive_landscape.title: Information-Theoretic Diffusion
competitive_landscape.difference: Kong et al. characterize diffusion through information-theoretic identities and objectives. This paper specializes conditional entropy into a practical inference-time time reparameterization derived from the existing denoising loss.

competitive_landscape.title: A Closer Look at Time Steps Is Worthy of Triple Speed-Up for Diffusion Model Training
competitive_landscape.difference: This work adapts timestep allocation to unequal learning importance for faster diffusion training. Entropic scheduling targets pretrained-model sampling and uses conditional information loss rather than empirical training progress, though its conclusion proposes extending the coordinate to training.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim conditional entropy and its rescaled/spectral variants provide canonical diffusion time coordinates that allocate equal information loss and improve few-step sampling without retraining.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Sections 4-5 derive invariance and estimation; Section 6 reports toy and EDM/EDM2 schedule comparisons.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The useful novelty is the training-loss-estimable global information coordinate and its strong first-order DDIM results. Optimized time grids, information-theoretic diffusion, spectral schedules, and adaptive timestep allocation are established. Raw entropy is not practically sufficient, rescaling is Gaussian-motivated, and solver dependence prevents treating the result as a universal canonical schedule.

reviewer_notes: Read all 31 pages of the pinned PDF, including time-change proofs, I-MMSE derivation, Gaussian optimum, solver limitations, complete CIFAR/FFHQ/ImageNet tables, reviewer-response material, and appendices. Primary arXiv records for optimized schedules, spectral allocation, information-theoretic diffusion, and timestep adaptation were checked on 2026-08-23. Raw-entropic failures and second-order negative results are retained rather than hidden behind the rescaled headline.
